problem: Foundation policies trained by imitation struggle on long-horizon mobile manipulation and navigation due to error accumulation. RL finetuning with sparse rewards suffers from credit assignment, and manually engineered dense rewards are task-specific, while per-step VLM rewards are too costly.
motivation: Long-horizon tasks need subgoal-level semantic supervision plus dense per-step feedback, without manual reward engineering. The authors observe that LLM/VLM progress estimates roughly track true progress but are noisy and expensive. They also propose that a pretrained policy's action-distribution self-certainty is a cheap dense proxy for task-consistent behavior.
key_idea: Use an LLM+scene-graph subgoal decomposition and VLM progress estimates only briefly to initialize the PPO value function, then finetune with a dense policy self-certainty intrinsic reward plus sparse task success reward.
insight: The two components are complementary. Ablation (Tab. 3): self-certainty mainly raises success, especially on OOD ObjNavAff (79.7 -> 89.7), and speeds convergence (best checkpoint ~30M vs 50M steps). VLM value initialization mainly raises SEL efficiency (Fetch SEL 54.7 -> 63.8). A tiny VLM budget (200K steps, <0.5% of training) suffices, and too large a self-certainty weight causes collapse.
method: LLM task decomposition: Claude-3.7-Sonnet maps (scene graph, instruction) to an ordered list of grounded subgoals with a fixed prompt.

VLM progress estimation: Amazon Nova Pro takes subgoals plus the previous and current frames and outputs progress p_t in [0,1]. It was chosen over CLIP and Qwen by comparing against A* rollouts. Reward is the increment of the running-maximum progress.

Premature-saturation prevention: after each rollout, a sliding-window median filter (window 9) zeroes isolated spikes where p_i minus the neighbor median exceeds a threshold (1/#subtasks), before computing the running maximum.
Value initialization (Stage I): the VLM reward supervises the critic for only 200K steps (<0.5% of 50M), then no more VLM queries.
Self-certainty intrinsic reward (Stage II): R_SC = -(1/|A|) sum_i log(|A| pi(i)) over the 20 discrete actions, a dense per-step reward measuring how peaked the action distribution is.
Final reward: R = alpha*1[StageI]*R_VLM + beta*1[StageII]*R_SC + phi*1[StageII]*R_task, with alpha=1, beta=0.1, phi=10, so sparse success anchors optimization.
PPO finetuning of SPOC following the FLaRe recipe, with 20M steps for ObjNav/RoomVisit and 50M for Fetch/PickUp/OOD tasks.

setting.backbone: SPOC pretrained IL policy finetuned with PPO; Claude-3.7-Sonnet (frozen) for decomposition and Amazon Nova Pro (frozen) for progress estimation
setting.training_data: SPOC IL pretraining data on CHORES, then online PPO in ProcTHOR houses (20M-50M steps; VLM value init 200K steps); no extra data
setting.observation: two egocentric RGB cameras (384x224, navigation and manipulator views) plus language instruction
setting.action_space: 20 discrete low-level actions (base translation/rotation, arm translation, gripper rotation, pickup, dropoff, done/terminate)
setting.privileged: Scene graph of the environment given to the LLM for subgoal decomposition, used during training only; none at test time

numbers_note: CHORES is not in the canonical list, so all rows use other:. The paper does not name the split beyond held-out test houses (10:1 split of ProcTHOR), so 'test' is used. Ablation numbers appear in Tab. 3 (SCR-only, VLM-only variants) and are not listed as separate rows.
results: VLLR beats FLaRe on all in-distribution tasks in success rate (ObjectNav 87.6 vs 85.0, Fetch 70.7 vs 65.23, PickUp 97.0 vs 91.8, RoomVisit 68.3 vs 60.87). FLaRe has slightly higher RoomVisit SEL (65.7 vs 64.8). On OOD tasks it reaches 67.4 on ObjNavRel (FLaRe 66.3) and 90.1 on ObjNavAff (FLaRe 79.7), also above SPOC++ trained with human-defined dense rewards. The abstract claims up to 56% absolute gain over the pretrained policy.
limitations: Evaluated only on the CHORES benchmark with a discrete action space; continuous-action manipulation is left to future work
Requires scene graphs for LLM decomposition and depends on noisy VLM progress estimates that need heuristic filtering; the VLM was chosen by qualitative comparison on one example
Gains over FLaRe are modest (about 1-10 points) with no reported seeds or variance, and the self-certainty weight must be balanced carefully to avoid collapse
